events.title: The Elegance of Erickson Exhibition
events.address: 124 West Main Street, Lancaster, Ohio 43130, United States of America
events.desc:
The Elegance of Erickson Exhibition is a celebration of handmade art glass by Carl Erickson and his team of glass masters at the Erickson Glass Works (1943-1961) in Bremen, Ohio. Erickson Glass Works was a renowned mid-century American studio art glass company. In 1906, at the age of 7, master glassblower Carl Erickson immigrated with his family from Reimyre, Sweden. He grew up in a family of master glassblowers, and at the age of 14, began his American career working as an apprentice alongside his father at the Pairpoint Manufacturing Company in New Bedford, Massachusetts.

 

The Ohio Glass Museum and Glass Blowing Studio is pleased to present this exhibition in honor of the Erickson Glass Works. The exhibition is made possible by the generous gifts of glass permanently donated to their archives by the following collectors: Elizabeth Norman, Paula and Rick Barnhart, Jeff Ulrich, Dave Shannon in memory of Faye Hillyard-Shannon. Visitors can view dynamic exhibits, watch daily live glassblowing demonstrations, shop for local handmade glass art, and participate in interactive studio classes in both glassblowing and fused glass. The Elegance of Erickson was curated by Michael Shook an

Curated by internationally recognized artist Nancy Crow, the exhibition at the Decorative Arts Center of Ohio includes works by quiltmakers from the United States, Canada, and New Zealand, highlighting the creativity, innovation and artistic excellence shaping contemporary quilt making today. Using bold abstract forms and richly worked fabrics, the artists balance exquisite skill with creative risk. Their quilts invite viewers to experience color as movement, texture, and feeling. This exhibition will run from October 3rd, 2026 to January 3rd, 2027.

 

For more information, please visit the Decorative Arts Center of Ohio’s website.

events.title: Spirit & Dust
events.desc:
“Death is a Dialogue between / The Spirit and the Dust,” writes poet Emily Dickinson. Living is a daily conversation with death, and through art, we continue that dialogue with mortality, loss, and our own humanity. In Spirit & Dust, artists working across various disciplines—from photography and sculpture to poetry and dance—seek to create space for care and connection in confronting questions of death and dying. What do we gather from our grief? How is this knowledge embodied, and what can art provide for this relationship? What can death teach us about what it means to be alive?

The process of creating art serves as a mirror for thinking about dying as a verb, where time is experienced as cyclical rather than linear. Each artist’s medium of choice in Spirit & Dust experiments with how we can deepen our relationship with the process of dying, such as through abstraction in photography, blank space in poetry, the ephemerality of dance, and the fallibility of materials in sculpture.

Spirit & Dust is on view concurrently with Experiencing Veterans and Artists Collaborations (EVAC) in the corridor space, which pairs veterans’ stories with original printmaking.

Curated by Diane Cal

events.address: 15 East Columbus Street, Pickerington, Ohio 43147, United States of America
events.desc:
Historian and Pickerington High alumnus Earl Nicodemus will discuss the incredible hardships faced by the 135th Ohio Volunteer Infantry during the American Civil War at this program in the Pickerington-Violet Township Historical Society Museum. After training at Camp Chase, located in what is now Columbus’ Hilltop, the troops, comprised of National Guard units from Licking and Hardin counties, were deployed to West Virginia to guard a railroad. A surprise Confederate attack led to the infantry’s capture. Many of the men would lose their lives, either during the insidious death march to the infamous Andersonville prison camp or while imprisoned there. Come enjoy this free presentation! Note: The Fall Pickerington High School Art Exhibit will also be on display at the museum from 2 p.m. to 4 pm.

For more information, please visit the Pickerington-Violet Township Historical Society’s Facebook page.

events.title: Spirit & Dust
events.desc:
“Death is a Dialogue between / The Spirit and the Dust,” writes poet Emily Dickinson. Living is a daily conversation with death, and through art, we continue that dialogue with mortality, loss, and our own humanity. In Spirit & Dust, artists working across various disciplines—from photography and sculpture to poetry and dance—seek to create space for care and connection in confronting questions of death and dying. What do we gather from our grief? How is this knowledge embodied, and what can art provide for this relationship? What can death teach us about what it means to be alive?

The process of creating art serves as a mirror for thinking about dying as a verb, where time is experienced as cyclical rather than linear. Each artist’s medium of choice in Spirit & Dust experiments with how we can deepen our relationship with the process of dying, such as through abstraction in photography, blank space in poetry, the ephemerality of dance, and the fallibility of materials in sculpture.

Spirit & Dust is on view concurrently with Experiencing Veterans and Artists Collaborations (EVAC) in the corridor space, which pairs veterans’ stories with original printmaking.

Curated by Diane Cal

events.title: NOVEL CONVERSATION
events.desc:
The Wind Knows My Name
by
Isabel Allende

Vienna, 1938. Samuel Adler was six years old when his father disappeared during Kristallnacht—the night their family lost everything. Samuel’s mother secured a spot for him on the last Kindertransport train out of Nazi-occupied Austria to the United Kingdom, which he boarded alone, carrying nothing but a change of clothes and his violin.

Arizona, 2019. Eight decades later, Anita Diaz, a blind seven-year-old girl, and her mother board another train, fleeing looming danger in El Salvador and seeking refuge in the United States. However, their arrival coincides with the new family separation policy, and Anita finds herself alone at a camp in Nogales. She escapes through her trips to Azabahar, a magical world of the imagination she created with her sister back home.

Anita’s case is assigned to Selena Duran, a young social worker who enlists the help of a promising lawyer from one of San Francisco’s top law firms. Together they discover that Anita has another family member in the United States: Leticia Cordero, who is employed at the home of now eighty-six-year-old Samuel Adler, linking these two lives.

Spanning time and place, The Wind Knows

Join the Fairfield County Heritage Association for their 2026 Fall Meeting as Tom O’Grady will be presenting “The Barn Builders: An Architectural Legacy in Ohio’s Rural Landscape.” Tickets are $20 each and can be purchased online today. Did you know that you can identify where people settled from in Ohio by the barns that they built? Barn builders left an architectural legacy that can help one understand much about the heritage of the region and the culture groups that migrated here. Tom O’Grady has been an instructor of Observational Astronomy at Ohio University for thirty years. He has spent a good deal of the past 25 years as a student of Ohio history researching its geography and settlement, the moundbuilders, Ohio canals, and several of its interesting characters and their stories. Guests will also enjoy coffee and a sundae bar from Whit’s Frozen Custard! The meeting will take place at 6:00 p.m. at the historic Lancaster Masonic Lodge.

events.title: Spirit & Dust
events.desc:
“Death is a Dialogue between / The Spirit and the Dust,” writes poet Emily Dickinson. Living is a daily conversation with death, and through art, we continue that dialogue with mortality, loss, and our own humanity. In Spirit & Dust, artists working across various disciplines—from photography and sculpture to poetry and dance—seek to create space for care and connection in confronting questions of death and dying. What do we gather from our grief? How is this knowledge embodied, and what can art provide for this relationship? What can death teach us about what it means to be alive?

The process of creating art serves as a mirror for thinking about dying as a verb, where time is experienced as cyclical rather than linear. Each artist’s medium of choice in Spirit & Dust experiments with how we can deepen our relationship with the process of dying, such as through abstraction in photography, blank space in poetry, the ephemerality of dance, and the fallibility of materials in sculpture.

Spirit & Dust is on view concurrently with Experiencing Veterans and Artists Collaborations (EVAC) in the corridor space, which pairs veterans’ stories with original printmaking.

Curated by Diane Cal

events.title: Spirit & Dust
events.desc:
“Death is a Dialogue between / The Spirit and the Dust,” writes poet Emily Dickinson. Living is a daily conversation with death, and through art, we continue that dialogue with mortality, loss, and our own humanity. In Spirit & Dust, artists working across various disciplines—from photography and sculpture to poetry and dance—seek to create space for care and connection in confronting questions of death and dying. What do we gather from our grief? How is this knowledge embodied, and what can art provide for this relationship? What can death teach us about what it means to be alive?

The process of creating art serves as a mirror for thinking about dying as a verb, where time is experienced as cyclical rather than linear. Each artist’s medium of choice in Spirit & Dust experiments with how we can deepen our relationship with the process of dying, such as through abstraction in photography, blank space in poetry, the ephemerality of dance, and the fallibility of materials in sculpture.

Spirit & Dust is on view concurrently with Experiencing Veterans and Artists Collaborations (EVAC) in the corridor space, which pairs veterans’ stories with original printmaking.

Curated by Diane Cal

events.title: Spirit & Dust
events.desc:
“Death is a Dialogue between / The Spirit and the Dust,” writes poet Emily Dickinson. Living is a daily conversation with death, and through art, we continue that dialogue with mortality, loss, and our own humanity. In Spirit & Dust, artists working across various disciplines—from photography and sculpture to poetry and dance—seek to create space for care and connection in confronting questions of death and dying. What do we gather from our grief? How is this knowledge embodied, and what can art provide for this relationship? What can death teach us about what it means to be alive?

The process of creating art serves as a mirror for thinking about dying as a verb, where time is experienced as cyclical rather than linear. Each artist’s medium of choice in Spirit & Dust experiments with how we can deepen our relationship with the process of dying, such as through abstraction in photography, blank space in poetry, the ephemerality of dance, and the fallibility of materials in sculpture.

Spirit & Dust is on view concurrently with Experiencing Veterans and Artists Collaborations (EVAC) in the corridor space, which pairs veterans’ stories with original printmaking.

Curated by Diane Cal

Or you may already have pretty penmanship, but desire to up your game so you can confidently hand-letter a custom script for gifts, events, décor, or other cherished items—art that can be proudly circulated and displayed. The art of “modern calligraphy” is more accessible than it looks, and we're here to help beginners learn the simple tools, strokes, and styles that can turn handwritten words into visual art. This workshop will cover basic tips and tricks for crafting lovely letters and words with everyday tools and techniques at your disposal—no fancy fountain pens, messy ink wells, or Gothic lettering knowledge required.

Your instructor, Martha Bove is a full-time college English instructor with a background heavy in poetry and painting. As an appreciator, teacher, and practitioner of words and art (and their convergence in calligraphy), she enjoys crafting custom lettering and design with others and for others.

Adults (18+) only, please.

events.title: James McNeill Whistler (Exhibition on Screen)
events.desc:
In an era of great change and great beauty emerged the character of James McNeill Whistler. Considered by some to be one of the great innovators of 19th century art, he was a contemporary of the Impressionists, much admired by Van Gogh and Manet. Boldly experimental and famously witty, Whistler disrupted the strict conventions of Victorian society in pursuit of a new cult of beauty, creating “art for art’s sake” and earning himself a place in the history of great art. He found a parallel between painting and music, and entitled many of his paintings “arrangements”, “harmonies” and “nocturnes”, emphasizing the importance of tonal harmony in his work. 
 
Tate Britain is now holding the first major retrospective of Whistler in three decades. This blockbuster exhibition promises to reawaken the world to just how important Whistler is to art history, uniting world-famous masterpieces with rarely seen works. 
 
Made in close collaboration with Tate Britain, directed by David Bickerstaff https://worthington.org/calendar.aspx?EID=9450

events.title: Spirit & Dust
events.desc:
“Death is a Dialogue between / The Spirit and the Dust,” writes poet Emily Dickinson. Living is a daily conversation with death, and through art, we continue that dialogue with mortality, loss, and our own humanity. In Spirit & Dust, artists working across various disciplines—from photography and sculpture to poetry and dance—seek to create space for care and connection in confronting questions of death and dying. What do we gather from our grief? How is this knowledge embodied, and what can art provide for this relationship? What can death teach us about what it means to be alive?

The process of creating art serves as a mirror for thinking about dying as a verb, where time is experienced as cyclical rather than linear. Each artist’s medium of choice in Spirit & Dust experiments with how we can deepen our relationship with the process of dying, such as through abstraction in photography, blank space in poetry, the ephemerality of dance, and the fallibility of materials in sculpture.

Spirit & Dust is on view concurrently with Experiencing Veterans and Artists Collaborations (EVAC) in the corridor space, which pairs veterans’ stories with original printmaking.

Curated by Diane Cal

events.desc:
In our lives, we are both always experts and novices. Personal essay and book-length memoirs allow writers to explore compelling, central moments, experiences, and material from their lives to communicate meaning, universal themes, and takeaways to readers, transforming experience into narrative art. What are the ethics of writing about others? We will explore conventions of the form, such as self-disclosure and deep examination, creating tension, character arc, using scenes and dialogue, distilling the “one big thing” your piece is about, and the blurry boundaries of fact and imagination in creative nonfiction—the only writing form defined by what it is not. Discussion questions may include: how do you maximize self-inquiry while avoiding “navel gazing”? What elements make stories engaging to readers? How do you craft a persona on the page?

By the end of the session, you will possess an understanding of personal essay and memoir writing fundamentals: honesty, self-reflection, tension, balancing scenes and exposition, distilling your memoir or essay’s “about-ness” (i.e., theme), and what to include versus what to omit. A timeless American classic, The Crucible explores the dangers of suspicion, the cost of integrity, and the courage it takes to stand by one’s convictions. Powerful, thought-provoking, and deeply relevant, this unforgettable play continues to resonate with audiences today. Tickets will sell quickly, so be sure to reserve your seat today! Join your Guiding Ohio Online Technology Trainer in a one-hour exploration of the best practices for keeping yourself safe while on the internet. You’ll learn what makes a secure password and why password security is so important, and how to keep your computer’s security software up to date. You’ll also learn how to recognize and defend against social engineering and learn some of the common scams you may encounter when using your computer or mobile device. 

Register online, on our app, or by calling (740) 653-2745, extension 160.

events.title: Rise Up Arts Alliance Presents: The Crucible
events.desc:
Rise Up Arts Alliance Presents: The Crucible on November 19th-22nd at the Lancaster City Parks office! Set during the Salem witch trials of 1692, The Crucible is Arthur Miller’s gripping drama about fear, power, and the consequences of mass hysteria. As accusations of witchcraft spread through a small Puritan town, neighbors turn against one another, reputations are destroyed, and impossible choices must be made in the pursuit of truth and justice. A timeless American classic, The Crucible explores the dangers of suspicion, the cost of integrity, and the courage it takes to stand by one’s convictions. Powerful, thought-provoking, and deeply relevant, this unforgettable play continues to resonate with audiences today. Tickets will sell quickly, so be sure to reserve your seat today! This show is recommended for teens and adults due to mature themes and intense dramatic content.

For more information, please visit Rise Up Arts Alliance’s Facebook page.

events.desc: Hear the Columbus Symphony Orchestra and Chorus, joined by a quartet of exceptional guest soloists, bring to life this masterpiece by the great Italian opera composer. events.title: Ordinary Woman
events.venue: Davidson Theater –  Riffe Center Theatre Complex
events.desc:
An extraordinary new musical featuring the songs of Sheryl Crow.

This world premiere and unique collaboration between CAPA, BalletMet and European production company ODD Continent reimagines Grammy-winner Sheryl Crow’s most powerful songs – from “Steve McQueen” to “Strong Enough” – through drama, ballet, and live on-stage music.

Ordinary Woman is the story of estranged midwestern sisters who must reconcile conflicting memories of the past when forced back together by environmental and social unrest.

Made in Columbus by a local and international team, including BalletMet artistic director Remi Wörtmeyer, Ordinary Woman plays a very limited run of three performances only. Don’t miss your chance to see it before the rest of the world!

Great for the whole family, this early literacy class will get children ages 2 - 5 excited about reading! events.address: 134 South Columbus Street, Lancaster, Ohio 43130, United States of America
events.desc:
Learn to create traditional Vanillekipferl from Austria with Danielle of the European Cottage Bakery at this workshop in Keller Market House! Vanillekipferl is a beloved traditional Christmas cookie made with nuts that has gained popularity in other countries. In this class, you’ll learn how to shape and roll the cookie dough into ropes and cut them individually to roll them out by hand for shaping, how to bake them, and how to cover them in sugar without breaking them and without sprinkling powder sugar on top. You will get your cookies all prepared here in the workshop, and then take them home to bake. You will need powdered sugar at home to finish.

You will also receive recipes to make marzipan from scratch and ideas for how to use it, plus a recipe to make Rumtopf (which takes a minimum of 3 months to create before using it) or dumplings. Tickets are $40 to the general public and $35 for friend of the market members. Register online today before seats sell out! The registration deadline is Saturday, November 28th. events.title: NOVEL CONVERSATION
events.desc:
The Stolen Life of Colette Marceau
by
Kristin Harmel

Colette Marceau has been stealing jewels for nearly as long as she can remember, following the centuries-old code of honor instilled in her by her mother, take only from the cruel and unkind, and give to those in need. Never was their family tradition more important than seven decades earlier, during the Second World War, when Annabel and Colette worked side by side in Paris to fund the French Resistance.

But one night in 1942, it all went wrong. Annabel was arrested by the Germans, and Colette’s four-year-old sister, Liliane, disappeared in the chaos of the raid, along with an exquisite diamond bracelet sewn into the hem of her nightgown for safekeeping. Soon after, Annabel was executed, and Liliane’s body was found floating in the Seine—but the bracelet was nowhere to be found.

Seventy years later, Colette—who has “redistributed” $30 million in jewels over the decades to fund many worthy organizations—has done her best to put her tragic past behind her, but her life begins to unravel when the long-missing bracelet suddenly turns up in a museum exhibit in Boston. If Colette can discover where it has been all this time—and who

events.title: Uptown Scrooge: Abridged!
events.desc:
A family friendly event! Step into the holiday hilarity of Uptown Scrooge: Abridged!, Good Medicine Productions’ wildly interactive twist on Charles Dickens’ beloved classic. This isn’t a show where you sit quietly in the dark—it’s a Christmas party where the audience becomes part of the story.

Filled with quick wit, outrageous characters, live music, and joyful audience participation, Uptown Scrooge delivers all the heart of Dickens with a healthy dose of laughter. Whether you’re cheering on Tiny Tim, booing Nephew Fred or finding yourself unexpectedly pulled into the action, every performance is a one-of-a-kind experience.

Perfect for families, homeschool groups, date nights, office parties, and anyone looking to laugh their way into the Christmas spirit, Uptown Scrooge:Abridged! reminds us that it’s never too late to choose generosity, joy & silliness.

events.title: Blood on the Clocktower
events.desc:
On a stormy night, a shriek echoes through the town. Everyone rushes to the clock tower to find their beloved storyteller has been murdered, lying still at its base. The villagers realize some evil has been unleashed on their town. By day, this evil looks like one of their own, but by night, it goes about, picking them off one by one. Can they identify the killer? Or will evil overrun this town in the end?

Blood on the Clocktower is an award-winning social deduction game in which a group of people works together to try to discover which one of them is the demon in their midst. During the game, you are either a "good" townsperson with roles that help you discover and share information with other "good" townspeople, or you are "evil" and try to sow lies and distrust among the other players. Each side wins when the other team is eliminated.

Each session usually runs 60 to 90 minutes. You can expect to:

Discover what Blood on the Clocktower is.

Learn how to play this game.

Meet new people through the cooperative gameplay.

Enjoy an afternoon of murder and mystery.

events.desc:

Unlike tutoring services that provide one-on-one help in specific subject areas, the Library’s Homework Help service supports students by ensuring they are able to complete specific work assigned by their classroom teachers.

events.title: ChronoShift Escape Room
events.desc:
What if you could go back in time and rewrite reality? In ChronoShift, you can!

A simple joke gone wrong—an AI-generated post meant for laughs spirals into a real-life disaster, derailing your friend’s hopes to be elected to the student council. Your mission? Travel back in time, change the flow of information, and fix the mistake. Can you undo the damage and repair your friendship? You’ll need to track down the AI-generated materials before they cause mayhem for your friends!

Developed by the Center for an Informed Public at the University of Washington, Loki's Loop creates activities designed to teach teens how to navigate complex information environments.

events.title: Portraits of Courage: A Commander in Chief’s Tribute to America’s Warriors
events.desc:
The National Veterans Memorial and Museum (NVMM) will host Portraits of Courage: A Commander in Chief’s Tribute to America’s Warriors, a collection of original paintings by former President George W. Bush. The exhibition opens to the public on August 8, 2026.

The exhibition features more than 60 portraits of post-9/11 service members and Veterans, each one hand painted by President Bush and paired with a personal story of service, sacrifice, and resilience written by the former president.

The NVMM is open Thursday through Sunday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.

events.title: Homework Help Center
events.desc:
The Homework Help Center is a community resource that serves the entire Pickerington Local School District. Unlike tutoring services that provide one-on-one help in specific subject areas, the Library’s Homework Help service supports students by ensuring they are able to complete specific work assigned by their classroom teachers. 

Library staff and volunteers are knowledgeable in guiding students through homework assignments in many subjects and grade levels. If the subject material is beyond the knowledge of staff and volunteers or students need more individual assistance than we can provide, we can direct them to resources for additional help.

Open Monday-Thursday following the PLSD calendar.

For more information and online resources, visit https://pickeringtonlibrary.org/homework-help-center/.

events.title: Make Herbal Holiday Magic at Keller Market House
events.address: 134 South Columbus Street, Lancaster, Ohio 43130, United States of America
events.desc:
Join Keller Market House for a festive, hands-on workshop where you’ll learn how to craft one-of-a-kind herbal gifts for your loved ones! Step into the warmth and beauty of the season in this festive herbal make-and-take workshop. Students will craft a gorgeous holiday bath soak layered in jars with botanicals, skin-loving clays, and magnesium salts, plus a fragrant simmer pot sachet filled with wintry herbs and spices to cozy the home with natural scent and seasonal cheer. Equal parts creative, practical, and delightful, this class is perfect for anyone who loves handmade gifts, herbal self-care, and bringing the comfort of the natural world into the holiday season.

Woodland Herbal will provide everything you need and you’ll leave with beautiful, meaningful presents made by your own hands. This is also an excellent experience to gift your loved ones and friends that you can do together! Tickets are $35 for the general public and $30 for friends of the market members. Register online today before tickets sell out! The registration deadline is Friday, December 11th. Be ready to laugh, learn and play!

For more information, please visit Keller Market House’s Facebook page.

events.title: Bricks & Banter: Ornaments
events.desc:
Unwind, get creative, and connect with others at Bricks & Banter—a monthly LEGO program just for adults (18+). Each session features a seasonally themed build you’ll assemble and take home. Whether you’re a lifelong builder or new to LEGO, this program is a fun, low-pressure way to relax, express your creativity, and meet fellow makers.

At this LEGO Club meeting, you will build gingerbread ornaments, complete with fun holiday details and creative surprises. Discover different ways to customize your gingerbread creations as you build a cheerful display perfect for the holiday season.

This event will be held at both the Pickerington Main Library and the Sycamore Plaza Library on the same night. Please note which location you registered for.

Registration required. Adults only.
